Software Engineer II @ SNC  |
Translating the Customer Vision into the Digital World
profile.summary: I'm a TS/SCI cleared Software Developer specializing in mission-critical C++ systems. With 3 years of experience in the defense sector, I work on the full software development lifecycle—translating customer capabilities into actionable requirements, into hardened, containerized C++ applications that communicate across distributed networks.

positions.title: Senior Associate Software Engineer
positions.description:
C++ Based Audio Processor
- Responsible for development and integration on 10+ platforms running 3 different operating systems.
- Containerized the processor using Podman resulting in a decrease in hardware requirements. 
- Researched and collaborated with a senior developer to implement Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) capabilities and display them on a GUI

- Communicated with internal customers to add new processors into the system.
- Collaborated with senior developers on my team to debug issues booting.

volunteerExperiences.description:
Fellowship, Leadership, Scholarship, and Service. 
Joining this chapter for my last two semesters at UTD was a vital part of my college career. I've gained business experience, philanthropic opportunities, networking, and leadership opportunities.

Alongside my brothers I volunteered 42 hours to help raise over $14,000 for veterans in need during our annual philanthropy event, Box-A-Thon. We built a cardboard house in the center of campus and lived out of it for the week, while collecting donations for Homes For Our Troops.

projects.title: Virtual Teaching Assistant
projects.description: For my Senior Design Project I am working in a team of 6 to architect a teaching assistant chatbot for the Advanced Algorithm Analysis course at UTD. We developed a web app with a chatbot using React, Flask, and Firebase. After considering the timeline and scope of our project, we decided to use ChatGPT 3.5 to integrate Artificial Intelligence into our chatbot, rather than building our own model. The back end team parses the user's question, and using LangChain and Word Embeddings to gather context from the textbook and pass it to a ChatGPT API call, resulting in 5 second responses. Alongside answering syllabus and textbook questions, one of our customer's requirements is to graph functions that would be found in the course. To solve this problem, we formatted the user's question in a way that our OpenAI model would return an interactive latex graph of the function that we can display to the user. As Product Owner, I facilitated weekly team meetings with the customer to gain new insights and feedback on our backlog and requirements.

projects.title: Cold Case Catcher
projects.description: I took the opportunity to apply to ACM Projects and was granted a spot of one of the ten teams for the Spring 2022 semester. Over the course of ten weeks my team of four employed strategies from the Agile Framework like a Kanban board and scrum meetings discussing our backlog, blockers, and goals for the week. Together we developed a web app using React for our frontend and NodeJS for the backend. The goal of the project was to bring public awareness to criminal cases that have gone cold across the country, and provide a place where communities could share information and foster solutions. I was a member of our backend team and focused on user authentication and developing the functionality for the user notebooks. We deployed a Firebase Database to implement user authentication and store cases, comments, and notebooks. Additionally we took advantage of Google’s Custom Search JSON API to provide users with the top 10 search results for each case. We ended the semester by presenting our project along with the other nine teams to 200 peers, consisting of UTD's ACM chapter, as well as anyone from the Engineering and Computer Science fields at UTD who wished to attend.
